title: A grid with indexers
description:
Write a 2D grid type with indexers and use it for a tiny game of life.

```
generation 0     generation 1
.#.              ...
.#.              ###
.#.              ...
```
hints: `public T this[int x, int y] { get => Inside(x, y) ? _cells[y * Width + x] : default!; set { ... } }` (lesson 7.01).
Count neighbours with two loops from -1 to 1, skipping (0, 0); the default for cells outside makes the edges simple.
requirements: `class Grid<T>` with `this[int x, int y]` get/set; reading outside the grid returns `default`, writing outside throws.
A second indexer `this[(int X, int Y) p]`.
`Step(Grid<bool>)` returns the next generation (a live cell with 2 or 3 live neighbours lives; a dead cell with 3 becomes alive).
stretch: Make the grid wrap around at the edges and run a glider for 8 generations.
